item.description: Public Star Parties are the heart of the Robert Ferguson Observatory—your monthly invitation to experience the wonder of the night sky like never before. Whether you’re a lifelong astronomy enthusiast or simply curious about what lies beyond our planet, these gatherings offer something magical for everyone. Each month includes a variety of engaging astronomy presentations led by our expert docents. You’ll hear fascinating stories about the cosmos and the science behind some of the objects you’ll soon be observing. These talks set the stage for an unforgettable night under the stars. Step outside into the darkness of Sugarloaf Ridge State Park, where the skies open up in breathtaking clarity. You’ll have the chance to explore the universe through three of RFO’s massive telescopes, each powerful enough to reveal extraordinary detail: lunar craters, planets, star clusters, glowing nebulae, distant galaxies, and more. item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org

item.title: John Prine Tribute with David Luning, Jason Crosby, Ben Dubin and Victoria George — Sun Oct 11, 6:00 PM — Occidental Center for the Arts
item.description:
David Luning returns to OCA for a special tribute celebrating John Prine's birthday. David will be joined by musical colleagues Jason Crosby, Ben Dubin and Victoria George. Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Get Tickets This show will take place in our auditorium. Doors open at 5:30 PM. David Luning knew at a young age the path his life should take. Throughout generations, troubadours and singers have harnessed the cultural landscape and passed it along, with the likes of John Prine and Townes Van Zandt paving the way with the telling of their stories. Following in those footsteps, the 29-year-old Sonoma County singer/songwriter's new record is the product of a massive turn in his life and taps into that cultural archive. Listening to ‘Souvenirs' by John Prine, was a cornerstone moment, compelling Luning to leave Berklee College and follow in the tradition of these iconic troubadours.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: SBC # 578 Debra Giusti, Entrepreneur & Speaker - Healing Cancer: An Integrative Path to Recovery & Prevention — Mon Oct 12, 6:00 PM — Hopmonk Sebastopol
item.description: A Personal Journey – After a recommendation for a double mastectomy (Stage 0 left breast and Stage 1 in right), Debra chose to investigate her options and developed a comprehensive integrative approach to significant recovery. She has experienced 100% healing in the left breast and 65%-70% in the right. Debra will talk about what she has learned about the root causes of cancer and factors that may influence cancer development and recovery. The potential of integrative approaches and the practical strategies she incorporated into her own healing program include nutrition, fasting, detoxification, supplementation, lifestyle changes, and supportive therapies. Using evidence as well as her own experience, Debra will identify and distinguish between established research, emerging evidence, and her own personal experience. The presentation offers an informative and hopeful look at what we know, what we are still learning, and how people can become more actively engaged in their own health.

item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
